bank.name: Physics
bank.subject: General Science & Ability
bank.description: Units, motion, forces, energy, light, sound, electricity, heat and the fundamentals of physics asked in CSS/GSA and one-paper exams.

questions.prompt: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.explanation: Force is measured in newtons (N).

questions.prompt: The SI unit of energy and work is?
questions.explanation: Work and energy are measured in joules (J).

questions.prompt: What is the SI unit of electric current?
questions.explanation: Electric current is measured in amperes (A).

questions.prompt: The SI unit of frequency is?
questions.explanation: Frequency is measured in hertz (Hz).

questions.prompt: What is the SI unit of pressure?
questions.explanation: Pressure is measured in pascals (Pa).

questions.prompt: The SI unit of electrical resistance is?
questions.explanation: Resistance is measured in ohms.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the SI unit of temperature?
questions.explanation: The SI unit of temperature is the kelvin (K).

questions.prompt: The speed of light in vacuum is approximately?
questions.explanation: Light travels at about 300,000 km/s (3 x 10^8 m/s) in vacuum.

questions.prompt: The speed of sound in air at room temperature is approximately?
questions.explanation: Sound travels at about 343 m/s in air at 20 C.

questions.prompt: In which medium does sound travel fastest?
questions.explanation: Sound travels fastest in solids because particles are closely packed.

questions.prompt: A rainbow is formed due to which phenomenon of light?
questions.explanation: Raindrops refract and disperse white light into its colours.

questions.prompt: The sky appears blue because of?
options: Scattering of light by air molecules
questions.explanation: Shorter blue wavelengths are scattered more by air molecules (Rayleigh scattering).

questions.prompt: Newton's first law of motion is also called the law of?
questions.explanation: Newton's first law states that a body at rest stays at rest unless acted on by a force: inertia.

questions.prompt: The equation F = ma represents Newton's?
questions.explanation: Newton's second law states force equals mass times acceleration.

questions.prompt: 'To every action there is an equal and opposite reaction' is Newton's?
questions.explanation: Newton's third law of motion describes action-reaction pairs.

questions.prompt: The kinetic energy of a moving body is given by?
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy = half times mass times velocity squared.

questions.prompt: Power is defined as?
questions.explanation: Power is the rate of doing work: work/time.

questions.prompt: At sea level, pure water boils at?
questions.explanation: Water boils at 100 C (212 F) at one atmosphere of pressure.

questions.prompt: Ice floats on water because?
options: Its density is lower than water
questions.explanation: Ice is less dense than liquid water, so it floats.

questions.prompt: Heat transfer by radiation does NOT require?
questions.explanation: Radiation (like sunlight) travels through vacuum without any medium.

questions.prompt: Like magnetic poles?
questions.explanation: Like poles repel; unlike poles attract.

questions.prompt: Ohm's law is expressed as?
questions.explanation: Voltage equals current times resistance.

questions.prompt: Which type of lens is used to correct short-sightedness (myopia)?
questions.explanation: Myopia is corrected with concave (diverging) lenses.

questions.prompt: Long-sightedness (hypermetropia) is corrected with?
questions.explanation: Hypermetropia is corrected with convex (converging) lenses.

questions.prompt: Nuclear reactors generate electricity through?
questions.explanation: Reactors use controlled nuclear fission of uranium or plutonium.

questions.prompt: The famous equation E = mc^2 was given by?
questions.explanation: Albert Einstein proposed the mass-energy equivalence in 1905.

questions.prompt: The gravity on the Moon is about what fraction of Earth's gravity?
questions.explanation: The Moon's gravity is about 1/6 that of Earth.

questions.prompt: Weight is the product of?
questions.explanation: Weight = mass x gravitational acceleration.

questions.prompt: Ultrasound refers to sound waves with frequency?
questions.explanation: Frequencies above 20,000 Hz are ultrasonic and are used in medical imaging.

questions.prompt: An ECG (electrocardiogram) records the activity of which organ?
questions.explanation: ECG records the electrical activity of the heart.

questions.prompt: The instrument used to measure atmospheric pressure is?
questions.explanation: A barometer measures atmospheric pressure.

questions.prompt: Which instrument measures the speed of wind?
questions.explanation: An anemometer measures wind speed.

questions.prompt: Convex mirrors are commonly used as?
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors give a wide field of view, ideal for rear-view mirrors.

questions.prompt: The image formed by a plane mirror is?
questions.explanation: Plane mirrors form virtual, erect, same-size images.

questions.prompt: The SI unit of electric charge is?
questions.explanation: Electric charge is measured in coulombs (C).

questions.prompt: A body in uniform circular motion has?
questions.explanation: Uniform circular motion involves centripetal acceleration towards the centre.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Force has both magnitude and direction, so it is a vector.

questions.prompt: Friction between two surfaces in contact can be reduced by?
questions.explanation: Lubricants reduce friction between moving parts.

questions.prompt: The bending of light as it passes from one medium to another is called?
questions.explanation: Refraction is the bending of light due to a change in medium.

questions.prompt: One newton is the force that accelerates a mass of 1 kg at a rate of:
questions.explanation: 1 N = 1 kg × 1 m/s².

questions.prompt: Which instrument measures electric potential difference (voltage)?
questions.explanation: A voltmeter measures the potential difference between two points.

questions.prompt: What is the SI unit of power?
questions.explanation: Power (rate of energy transfer) is measured in watts (W); the joule measures energy.

questions.prompt: Which scientist formulated the theory of general relativity?
questions.explanation: Einstein published the general theory of relativity in 1915, describing gravity as curved spacetime.

questions.prompt: Which device converts mechanical energy into electrical energy?
questions.explanation: A generator converts mechanical energy to electrical; a motor does the reverse.

questions.prompt: Which wave type does NOT require a medium to travel?
questions.explanation: Electromagnetic waves (light, radio) travel through a vacuum; mechanical waves need a medium.

questions.prompt: What happens to a gas when its temperature increases at constant pressure?
questions.explanation: Charles's Law: at constant pressure, gas volume is directly proportional to absolute temperature.

questions.prompt: The bending of light as it passes around an obstacle is called:
questions.explanation: Diffraction is the spreading/bending of waves around obstacles; refraction is bending through a medium.

questions.prompt: Which color of visible light has the shortest wavelength?
questions.explanation: Violet has the shortest wavelength and highest frequency in the visible spectrum.

questions.prompt: One watt is equal to one:
questions.explanation: 1 W = 1 J/s, so power is joules per second.

questions.prompt: An object at rest will remain at rest unless acted on by:
questions.explanation: Newton's first law: bodies maintain state unless an external force acts.

questions.prompt: Which force keeps planets orbiting the Sun?
questions.explanation: Gravity provides the centripetal force for planetary orbits.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
questions.explanation: Speed has magnitude only; the others also have direction.

questions.prompt: An electric generator converts:
questions.explanation: Generators convert mechanical energy into electricity.

questions.prompt: Which colour of light has the highest frequency?
questions.explanation: Violet has the highest frequency in the visible spectrum.

questions.prompt: A magnifying glass is an example of a:
questions.explanation: A convex (converging) lens magnifies close objects.

questions.prompt: The centre of the Earth is known as the:
questions.explanation: The Earth's innermost layer is the core.

questions.prompt: The resistance of a conductor depends on its:
questions.explanation: Resistance depends on length, cross-sectional area and resistivity.

questions.prompt: Which particle has a negative charge?
questions.explanation: Electrons carry a negative charge.

questions.prompt: Which simple machine is a screwdriver?
questions.explanation: A screwdriver works as a wheel and axle.

questions.prompt: The freezing point of water is:
questions.explanation: Water freezes at 0°C under standard conditions.

questions.prompt: The law of conservation of energy states that energy:
options: Cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed
questions.explanation: Energy is conserved; it only changes form.

questions.prompt: The SI unit of electric potential difference is:
questions.explanation: Voltage is measured in volts.

questions.prompt: Which instrument measures the speed of a vehicle?
questions.explanation: A speedometer shows a vehicle's speed.

questions.prompt: The phenomenon of sound bouncing back from a surface is called:
questions.explanation: An echo is reflected sound.

questions.prompt: Which lens is thicker at the centre than at the edges?
questions.explanation: A convex lens bulges at the centre.

questions.prompt: A magnet has how many poles?
questions.explanation: Every magnet has a north and a south pole.

questions.prompt: Which type of energy does a stretched bow possess?
questions.explanation: A stretched bow stores elastic potential energy.

questions.prompt: The phenomenon of magnetism produced by electric current is called:
questions.explanation: Electric current creates magnetic fields.

questions.prompt: Which instrument measures humidity?
questions.explanation: A hygrometer measures humidity.

questions.prompt: The instrument used to measure the density of liquids is:
questions.explanation: A hydrometer measures liquid density.

questions.prompt: The phenomenon of a rainbow is due to:
questions.explanation: Rainbows form by refraction and dispersion in water droplets.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a renewable energy source?
questions.explanation: Solar energy is renewable.

questions.prompt: The process by which a liquid changes into a gas at its surface is:
questions.explanation: Evaporation occurs at the liquid surface.

questions.prompt: The unit of magnetic flux density is:
questions.explanation: Tesla is the SI unit of magnetic flux density.

questions.prompt: The number of vibrations per second is called:
questions.explanation: Frequency counts oscillations per second.

questions.prompt: The pitch of sound depends on its:
questions.explanation: Pitch is determined by frequency.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a good insulator?
questions.explanation: Rubber does not conduct electricity well.

questions.prompt: Which scientist formulated the laws of motion?
questions.explanation: Newton formulated the three laws of motion.

questions.prompt: The rate of change of velocity is called:
questions.explanation: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity.

questions.prompt: The SI unit of mass is:
questions.explanation: Mass is measured in kilograms.

questions.prompt: The SI unit of time is:
questions.explanation: The second is the SI unit of time.

questions.prompt: What is the charge of an electron?
questions.explanation: An electron carries a negative charge of about 1.6 x 10^-19 coulombs.

questions.prompt: What happens to the pressure of a gas when its volume decreases at constant temperature?
questions.explanation: By Boyle's law, at constant temperature the pressure of a gas increases as its volume decreases.

questions.prompt: The process of converting a solid directly into gas is called:
questions.explanation: Sublimation is the direct change of a solid into vapour, e.g. dry ice or camphor.

questions.prompt: Which instrument measures electric current?
questions.explanation: An ammeter measures electric current in amperes; a voltmeter measures potential difference.

questions.prompt: Energy possessed by a moving body is called:
questions.explanation: The energy of motion is kinetic energy, given by 1/2 mv2.

questions.prompt: The phenomenon of splitting white light into colours is called:
questions.explanation: Dispersion splits white light into its spectrum, as seen in a prism or a rainbow.

questions.prompt: A concave lens always forms which type of image?
questions.explanation: A concave (diverging) lens always forms a virtual, erect and diminished image.

questions.prompt: Which type of wave is light?
questions.explanation: Light is a transverse electromagnetic wave and does not require a medium.

questions.prompt: The acceleration due to gravity on Earth is approximately:
questions.explanation: The standard value of g near the Earth's surface is about 9.8 m/s2.

questions.prompt: Which device converts sound waves into electrical signals?
questions.explanation: A microphone converts sound into electrical signals; a loudspeaker does the reverse.

questions.prompt: The normal human eye focuses images on the:
questions.explanation: The lens of the eye focuses light on the retina, where the image is formed.

questions.prompt: Which device is used to see distant objects clearly?
questions.explanation: A telescope magnifies distant objects; a microscope magnifies tiny nearby objects.

questions.prompt: The device used to measure electric power is:
questions.explanation: A wattmeter measures electric power in watts.

questions.prompt: Which metal is the best conductor of electricity?
questions.explanation: Silver is the best conductor of electricity, followed by copper.

questions.prompt: A transformer is used to:
questions.explanation: A transformer changes the voltage of alternating current (step-up or step-down).

questions.prompt: When a ray of light enters a denser medium, it bends:
questions.explanation: Light bends towards the normal when entering a denser medium, e.g. from air to water.

questions.prompt: A person's weight is less on the Moon because:
options: The Moon has less mass than the Earth
The Moon has weaker gravity than the Earth
The Moon is far from the Sun
questions.explanation: The Moon's gravity is about one-sixth of Earth's, so weight (mg) is about one-sixth.

questions.prompt: An electric motor converts:
questions.explanation: A motor converts electrical energy into mechanical energy; a generator does the reverse.

questions.prompt: The loudness of sound depends on its:
questions.explanation: Loudness depends on the amplitude of the sound wave; pitch depends on frequency.

questions.prompt: Which type of mirror is used in a shaving mirror?
questions.explanation: A concave mirror forms a magnified, erect image when the face is held close, which is ideal for shaving.

questions.prompt: The SI unit of luminous intensity is?
questions.explanation: Luminous intensity is measured in candelas (cd), one of the seven SI base units.

questions.prompt: The SI unit of magnetic flux is?
questions.explanation: Magnetic flux is measured in webers (Wb); flux density is measured in teslas.

questions.prompt: A fuse wire is generally made of an alloy of?
questions.explanation: Fuse wire uses a tin-lead alloy with a low melting point so it melts and breaks the circuit on overload.

questions.prompt: The SI unit of capacitance is?
questions.explanation: Capacitance is measured in farads (F).

questions.prompt: The SI unit of inductance is?
questions.explanation: Inductance is measured in henries (H).

questions.prompt: Which substance has the highest specific heat capacity?
questions.explanation: Water has a high specific heat capacity of about 4200 J per kg per kelvin, which is why it is used as a coolant.

questions.prompt: Convection is the main mode of heat transfer in?
questions.explanation: Convection transfers heat through the bulk movement of fluids, that is liquids and gases.

questions.prompt: Heat from the Sun reaches the Earth by?
questions.explanation: Radiation does not require a medium, so the Sun's heat crosses empty space by radiation.

questions.prompt: Which device is used to detect the presence of electric charge?
questions.explanation: An electroscope indicates electric charge by the divergence of its gold leaves.

questions.prompt: What is the frequency of AC mains supply in Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Pakistan's AC mains supply runs at 50 hertz, like most of Europe and Asia.

questions.prompt: Sound waves cannot travel through?
questions.explanation: Sound needs a material medium; it cannot travel through a vacuum.

questions.prompt: Which mirror is used in the headlights of vehicles?
questions.explanation: A concave mirror behind the bulb reflects a parallel beam of light ahead of the vehicle.

questions.prompt: A body is said to be in equilibrium when the net force acting on it is?
questions.explanation: In equilibrium the vector sum of all forces and torques acting on a body is zero.

questions.prompt: The turning effect of a force about a point is called?
questions.explanation: Torque, or moment of force, is the product of force and the perpendicular distance from the pivot.

questions.prompt: Which instrument measures the depth of the sea using sound waves?
questions.explanation: A fathometer sends sound pulses to the seabed and measures the echo time to find depth.

questions.prompt: The SI unit of plane angle is?
questions.explanation: The radian (rad) is the SI unit of plane angle.

questions.prompt: The SI unit of solid angle is?
questions.explanation: The steradian (sr) is the SI unit of solid angle.

questions.prompt: A sound wave is an example of a?
questions.explanation: In sound, particles vibrate parallel to the direction of propagation, so sound is a longitudinal wave.

questions.prompt: The formation of a mirage is due to?
questions.explanation: A mirage appears when light is totally internally reflected by hot, less dense layers of air near the ground.

questions.prompt: Which force opposes the relative motion of two surfaces in contact?
questions.explanation: Friction always opposes the relative sliding motion between two surfaces in contact.

questions.prompt: The strength of an electromagnet can be increased by?
options: Increasing the number of turns of the coil
questions.explanation: Field strength rises with more turns of wire, a larger current and a soft iron core.

questions.prompt: Kilowatt-hour (kWh) is a unit of?
questions.explanation: The kilowatt-hour is the commercial unit of electrical energy.

questions.prompt: The motion of a swinging pendulum is an example of?
questions.explanation: A pendulum repeats its motion at regular intervals, which is periodic motion.

questions.prompt: Which lens converges parallel rays of light to a single point?
questions.explanation: A convex (converging) lens brings parallel rays of light to a focus.

questions.prompt: An electric iron works on which effect of electric current?
questions.explanation: The heating effect of current is used in electric irons, heaters and toasters.

questions.prompt: The magnetic effect of an electric current was discovered by?
questions.explanation: In 1820 Oersted found that a current-carrying wire deflects a compass needle, showing the magnetic effect of current.

questions.prompt: Which colour of light is deviated the most when white light passes through a prism?
questions.explanation: Violet has the shortest wavelength and is deviated most during dispersion.

questions.prompt: The focal length (f) of a spherical mirror is related to its radius of curvature (R) by?
questions.explanation: The focus lies halfway between the pole and the centre of curvature, so f = R/2.

questions.prompt: The image formed on a cinema screen is?
questions.explanation: A projector forms a real, inverted image on the screen, which appears upright to the audience.
